title: Five More Sources: The Places the Route Almost Forgot | vitalii.no
description:
Why some places along a daily route stayed permanently silent, and how a nightly research pass gives them one more chance to be told.

Some places never got a story because the original harvest — a local-history wiki and a geosearch — simply didn't have enough written about them. A place that got skipped stayed skipped forever; there was no mechanism to go looking for more before giving up on it.

A new research script now runs on its own nightly schedule, separate from the writer, so it costs no extra API calls. It takes places that were passed over on at least two of the last twenty-one days without a story and digs further: digitised local newspapers from the National Library, full-text mentions on the local-history wiki, historical reference books, and encyclopedia entries, all with ads and scanning noise filtered out. It also checks nearby Wikidata records within 150 meters of the track and promotes forgotten spots — old dairies, mills, factories, stumbling stones — into new places on the route whenever there's enough material to say something real.

Places that used to sit silent forever now get a second, deeper pass through five additional real sources before being given up on.
